_comment: Source of truth for MinIO service accounts on the self-hosted cluster (#813).
Read by infra/hetzner/provision-minio-users.sh (creates users/policies/Secrets),
infra/hetzner/verify-minio-scoping.sh (the allow/deny assertions), and
scripts/check_hetzner_minio_credentials.py (the committed-file guard).
JSON, not YAML, so every consumer parses it with the Python stdlib and no
workstation needs pyyaml installed.
`allow` and `deny` together must name every bucket in `all_buckets` for each
account: an unlisted bucket is an untested bucket, and the guard fails on it.
`access` is derived from what the workload's code actually does — see the table in
infra/hetzner/README.md and the file:line citations in the #813 PR body:
ro = s3:GetObject only
wo = s3:PutObject / DeleteObject / AbortMultipartUpload / ListMultipartUploadParts
rw = both
Bucket-level s3:ListBucket / GetBucketLocation / ListBucketMultipartUploads are
granted for every allowed bucket regardless of `access`.
`prefix` is the object-key prefix the account is scoped to inside that bucket. The
policy document's object-level Resource must be exactly
arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/<prefix>* — the guard asserts that, and derives the probe keys
verify-minio-scoping.sh uses from it, so a probe can never land outside the granted
prefix and pass vacuously.
KNOWN GAP — di-consumer + Iceberg (ADR-0036). di-consumer's lakehouse grant is
scoped to canonical/, which is where the Delta sink writes. The Iceberg sink
(persist/sinks.py IcebergCanonicalSink) reuses the SAME DI_S3_* credential against the
Nessie warehouse root s3://evidara-lakehouse, which is OUTSIDE canonical/. That path is
inert today (DI_ICEBERG_CATALOG_URI is unset in apps/configmap.yaml), but whoever
enables it must widen di-consumer's `prefix` to "" and di-consumer.json's object
Resource to arn:aws:s3:::evidara-lakehouse/*, or the first write returns AccessDenied.
The MinIO root credential (Secret `minio-root`) is administrative only. No workload
may reference it. The `console` MinIO user is NOT managed here — audit it separately;
see Step 6 of docs/runbooks/minio-least-privilege-cutover.md.
